@@ -72549,6 +72556,22 @@ Demos: +
:user-valid
body:
Hmm. I see three options here:

1. `:user-valid` does not work on FACE. This is because we honestly admit that it's just not hooked up. Maybe in the future we'll work on a custom API for hooking it up better.

2. `:user-valid` on FACEs is the same as `:valid`.
   - Pro: avoids web developers having to do weird selectors like `:user-valid, my-face:valid { ... }` if they have shared styles for both cases.
   - Con: might make `:user-valid` less trustworthy. (In particular, you might be sad to get "random" red boxes applied to your FACEs on page load, when using `:user-invalid { border: 1px solid red; }`.)

3. We try to do some cool magic. Something like: if the control fires a `change` event at itself, we flip the flag.

All cases can be made to work with a future extension API. (1) is perhaps the most straightforward, since then the future extension API is just `elementInternals.setUserHasInteractedForValidityPurposes()`. (2) and (3) would probably require some mechanism for opting in to more manual control.
